subject.title: Feature: Session authentication PIN gate (framework-level tool blocking)

question: Should session PIN gating be a core OpenClaw security primitive, or should it remain an external plugin/ClawHub pattern built on `before_tool_call` plus session extensions?
rationale: Current main has enough hook and session primitives for an external implementation, but the requested behavior adds core auth configuration, secret handling, trusted verification semantics, and default security policy that automation should not choose.

options.title: Core session-auth primitive
options.body: Add a core-owned session auth mode with trusted verifier, session state, reset semantics, docs, and upgrade-safe configuration handling.

options.title: External plugin pattern
options.body: Document or publish the capability as a plugin/ClawHub package using current hook and session-extension APIs, without adding core config.

options.title: Defer to broader guardrails work
options.body: Keep this open until the related guardrail and step-up authorization designs settle the common security boundary.

recommendation.title: Core session-auth primitive
recommendation.body: Add a core-owned session auth mode with trusted verifier, session state, reset semantics, docs, and upgrade-safe configuration handling.

likelyOwner.reason: The most relevant current-main blame and history samples for before-tool-call, session state, and reset lifecycle point to steipete, and the issue timeline also mentions him for maintainer feedback.
